clue.text: Seek person (eg God) with honest intention, otherwise one will be milling and not stopping with the hooter

definitions.text: milling and not stopping with the hooter

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are to be set out in another order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, the bracketed eg and God included
taken letter for letter

annotation.spelling: KEEPING ONE'S NOSE TO THE GRINDSTONE

explanation.surface: A sermon-like urging to seek God sincerely, set against a worker grinding away without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirty letters of the first and last phrases, joined by 'with', rearrange into the idiom. Hooter is slang for the nose, and a grindstone mills.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means working hard without rest; the setter pictures it literally, a grinding mill with a face pressed continually against it.

clue.text: To get curtailed during vocal — such a one should be shot!

definitions.text: such a one should be shot
definitions.note: describes the person rather than giving an adjective

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut short, so the final letter of the word before is dropped
during means within the span of, so the shortened words sit inside the word for vocal

parts.note: phonic means relating to the voice or speech sounds
the two words run together, minus the last letter of get

explanation.surface: A gleeful call for some unfortunate singer to be shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests execution, but shot here means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks good in photographs deserves to be captured by a camera, which is the sense of shot used here.

clue.text: Verbal rules, with string attached, on sheep locking horns?

parts.note: the G string of a violin
a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: two animals locking horns face each other, so the second of the pair is turned to point the other way

parts.note: a second male sheep, facing the first

explanation.surface: A fanciful picture of two rams butting heads with a string tied on.
explanation.walkthrough: One sheep word serves twice: the pair of rams meet head to head, so one reads forwards and one backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is the set of rules governing how words are combined in a language, hence rules about verbal usage.

clue.text: This is the way to cover chicks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the direction this very clue runs in the grid
second meaning: the fine fluffy feathers on young birds

explanation.surface: Advice on how to keep baby birds warm.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the way points at the clue itself, which is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue sits in the down column, and soft fluffy feathers covering young birds are also called by the same word.

clue.text: Having left the terrible Times, here's what we're going on about

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to the set phrase going about our lawful occasions

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a direct synonym
occasions are particular times

explanation.surface: Someone who has walked out on the dreadful Times newspaper explains what they are now complaining about.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Times look like the newspaper. The naval prayer speaks of those who pass on the seas upon their lawful occasions, and to go about one's lawful occasions is to mind one's own legitimate business.
explanation.definitionFit: The set phrase going about our lawful occasions names the ordinary legitimate business people pursue, so it is what we are going about.

clue.text: Big breakfast eater getting his …

parts.note: surface reading: someone tucking into a large morning meal
setter's reading: a huge figure restored after eating, with the clue running on into the next one

explanation.surface: A hearty eater sitting down to a full fried breakfast, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is from Psalm 78, 'like a giant refreshed with wine'; the ellipsis hands the sentence on to 14-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge person who has just eaten is restored and reinvigorated, which is the psalm's image of a mighty figure revived.

clue.text: Flier in liquor to pour the tea

indicators.note: in places the flying creature within the drink word

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink
a moth is a flying insect

explanation.surface: An insect has fallen into someone's drink at a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: To be mother is a British idiom for being the one who pours the tea for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the person serving tea from the pot is said to play mother, an informal domestic idiom.

clue.text: Colour known as point-blank?

parts.note: surface reading: shooting from very close
setter's reading: a range of nothing, the blank being the round zero letter

explanation.walkthrough: Point-blank range means a range of zero, and zero written as the letter O placed before the word for distance gives the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the colour between red and yellow in the spectrum, named after the citrus fruit.

clue.text: What happens when you aim for the stars?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the outcome or result

definitions.text: when you aim for the stars
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a shot fired skywards

explanation.walkthrough: Aiming for the stars sounds like ambition; read literally it is firing a shot into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the final result or outcome of events, and split in two it is a shot directed skyward.

clue.text: Iberian transsexual in Jane's?

parts.note: surface reading: a Spaniard or Portuguese person who has changed sex
setter's reading: the Portuguese sea creature, and a warship listed in Jane's Fighting Ships, called man but referred to as she

explanation.surface: A Spanish or Portuguese trans person mentioned in some magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane's Fighting Ships is the standard reference book on navies. Ships are called she, so a warship named man is a male turned female, and the Portuguese one is a jellyfish-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old armed sailing warship, the kind of vessel catalogued in naval reference annuals, and also the stinging Portuguese siphonophore.

clue.text: Weapons returned, as is very well fitting

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: guns are weapons

explanation.surface: Weapons sent back because they fit very well, an odd reason for a return.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug describes clothing that is close-fitting and comfortable, sitting tightly on the body without being loose.

clue.text: G-girl clergy, there for the washing up

definitions.note: describes the cloth's purpose rather than naming it

parts.note: the letter as printed
lass is a word for a girl
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: A stammering girl and a clergyman helping in the kitchen after a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: G-girl looks like a stutter, but the G is simply a letter to take as it stands. Washing up is British for washing the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass cloth is a linen towel used to dry and polish glasses and dishes after they are washed.

clue.text: … small-time twist, allowing further effort

definitions.note: describes what the thing does rather than naming it

parts.note: a second is a small unit of time
to wind is to twist or coil

explanation.surface: The giant of 7-down, after breakfast, gets a small twist that lets him keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 7-down: a giant refreshed gets his second wind, and the psalm's giant was refreshed with wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is renewed energy that lets someone continue exerting themselves after tiring, as in a long race.

clue.text: Least divided of France's ports?

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is one of them

indicators.note: divided asks for the word before to be split into two parts, each clued separately

parts.note: the first letter of the split word, kept as it stands
the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A question about which French port is least split or disputed.
explanation.walkthrough: Least reads as the superlative, but it splits as L plus east. Lorient is a naval port in Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorient is a port town on the Brittany coast of France, so it is one of the country's harbours.

clue.text: Being illiterate, I'm on my bike with hangers-on in the cold

indicators.note: someone who cannot spell writes words as they hear them, so the phrase is spelt by its sound

parts.note: riding a bike is cycling, put in the first person ungrammatically

explanation.surface: An uneducated cyclist rides through freezing weather with others tagging along.
explanation.walkthrough: Hangers-on suggests followers, but it means things hanging from eaves in the frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Icicles are spikes of ice that hang from roofs and gutters in freezing weather, literally hanging on in the cold.

clue.text: Stir it when there's an entry to the outside

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: being to the outside means surrounding, so the entry word wraps around the small word

parts.note: a gate is a way in
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to stir something whenever a door to the outside appears.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate a liquid is to stir or shake it so that it moves about vigorously.

clue.text: Female a month ago reached Pole, making an unusual figure

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
Dec is the abbreviation for December
taken as written
N for the North Pole

explanation.surface: A woman reached the Pole a month ago, an unusual feat.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure looks like a person or a number, but here it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A hendecagon is an eleven-sided polygon, a geometric shape seldom met compared with hexagons or octagons.

clue.text: Peculiar character of gold removed from the Lights

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of it, leaving the remaining letters

parts.note: the aurora is the display of northern or southern lights
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A strange quality of gold has gone missing from the lights.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold tempts AU, but here it is the heraldic OR, taken out of the middle of the lights.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality surrounding a person or place, a special air about them.

clue.text: A number entered during a spell of work needing no thought

definitions.note: describes the noun rather than naming it

parts.note: in as in in the course of

indicators.note: something that has entered has gone inside, so the number goes within the work word

parts.note: a stint is a period of work
C is the Roman numeral 100

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a mindless stretch of work during which a number came in.
explanation.walkthrough: A number is a hundred in Roman numerals, slipped inside the stretch of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is innate behaviour that happens automatically, without conscious reasoning or deliberate reflection.

clue.text: Work with your hands saying what you should have

indicators.note: saying means speaking the word, so it is the sound that counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: to knead dough is to work it with the hands

explanation.surface: A craftsman's maxim about what you ought to possess.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a requirement, something a person ought to have or must obtain.

clue.text: Whatever I fancy doing, I use one hand, within reason

indicators.note: within puts the first pieces inside the word for reason

parts.note: the why of something is its reason
taken as written
a manuscript, abbreviated MS, is written by hand

explanation.surface: Someone doing exactly what they like, but within reason, even one-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: MS is the standard abbreviation for manuscript, a document written by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsy is acting on capricious fancy, doing whatever playful notion comes to mind at the moment.

clue.text: Time allowed for payment: what an _____ , says the creditor

indicators.note: says points to spoken words, so the gap is filled by what the lender's exclamation sounds like

parts.note: the creditor's annoyed exclamation, run together

explanation.surface: A lender grumbles about having to grant extra time for repayment.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, what a nuisance can be heard as what an usance.
explanation.definitionFit: Usance is the customary period allowed for paying a foreign bill of exchange, a technical banking term.

clue.text: Occupied by nurse before breaking in

indicators.note: breaking in means forcing a way inside, so one word ends up within the other

parts.note: to tend a patient is to nurse them
ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: A building occupied by a nurse before a burglar breaks in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenanted property is occupied by people renting it, so it is lived in rather than standing empty.
